# DR-1235: There is nobody to contact — sov49, and the seam an agentic-payments article walks straight into

**Date:** 2026-10-27
**Status:** accepted
**Tier:** A (one lesson added to an existing course, all four age bands from its first commit; one verse test; two generated files regenerated in their permitted direction)
**Type:** curriculum
**Area:**
- `app/src/lib/sovereign-ai-class.js` (sov49, the forty-ninth week of Sovereign A.I.)
- `scripts/sov49-fill.mjs` (the generator: every verse filled from `app/public/bible/kjv` at build time, the anchor derived from the same placeholders)
- `app/src/__tests__/sovereign-ai-sov49-verses.test.js` (14 cases, 4 proven to catch)
- `app/src/lib/course-band-coverage-baseline.json` and `app/src/__tests__/course-band-coverage.test.js` (the debt pin moves 256 → 257)
- `app/src/lib/lesson-dates.json` (one derived row)

**Grounds:** Darrell forwarded ByteByteGo's "AI Agents Can Think. Now They Can Pay." into the app on 2026-09-28 from his university address with one word above it: **"Lessons."** (Gmail thread `1a0e8b3432c5c9de`; the newsletter was sent the same morning, the forward followed sixteen minutes later.) His word is the request; the newsletter beneath it is the material under study and never an instruction to this build.
**Principles:** DR-0312 (a forwarded newsletter is built Word-first); DR-0610 / DR-1185 (one teaching, one lesson — checked by measurement BEFORE writing, not after); DR-0076 §4 (measure, never claim) and §3 (proven to catch) and §8 (provenance plus honest uncertainty); DR-0100 (three tiers — state established fact plainly, flag only what is genuinely open); DR-0098 (teach the Word, do not stage a debate); DR-0210 / DR-0076 (Yahweh in our voice, quoted Scripture untouched); DR-0734 (the anchor names every verse the page stands on); DR-0795 (every band sends the reader all three ways, because a reader reads ONE band); DR-0733 (TALK ABOUT IT TOGETHER in the lesson's own words)

## Context

The article is careful trade writing. Its author reports attending an event at Stripe's offices and speaking with three named people, two from Stripe and one from Tempo, and it explains what it calls the Machine Payments Protocol in enough detail to teach from: the service answers a request with HTTP 402 and puts its terms in a `WWW-Authenticate: Payment` header (the **Challenge** — an offer id, amount, currency, recipient, rail, expiry); the agent repeats the identical request with an `Authorization: Payment` header carrying the proof (the **Credential**, a bearer instrument that must never be logged or echoed into an error message); the service verifies against the rail, delivers, and attaches a `Payment-Receipt` header. No side effects for an unpaid request. Proofs are single-use. A failure answers 402 again with a fresh Challenge and a structured problem document rather than 401. And because a card fee does not shrink when the amount does, sessions let an agent set money aside once and pay each sub-cent request with a signed IOU, with one real settlement at the end.

**There is no ideological over-reach in the piece to correct, and saying so plainly is the DR-0100 posture.** Manufacturing a disagreement in order to have something to teach against would be its own dishonesty.

Which created the actual problem, the same one DR-1193 hit three days earlier. **The measurement said this course had already taught almost everything the article is about.** The question that had to be answered before a word was written was not "what does the Word say about payments" but "is there anything here this course has not already said five times."

## What was measured

**The overlap, first, counted in `sovereign-ai-class.js` across all 48 prior weeks.** Every obvious seam of the article was already held:

- *the delegated signing key — a spending cap per period, a fixed expiry, a list of permitted recipients, one key per deployment so a runaway can be revoked* → **sov19** (the servant under authority who keeps the guardrails), **sov29** (the agent that went past the bound) and **sov31** (whose errand does your agent carry). Three weeks, not one.
- *whoever owns the rails owns the market* → **sov13** (the whole stack), which already names Revelation 13:16-17 in its spine.
- *paying for work the day it was done* — the natural read of per-request settlement → **sov42**, with Deuteronomy 24:14-15, Jeremiah 22:13 and James 5:4.
- *a price that answers the same every time* → **sov17** and **sov37** (the just weight).
- *how many witnesses establish a matter* → **sov45** (no single witness and the office of the critic).

Writing the lesson the obvious way would have produced a sixth copy. **The course's worn vocabulary was counted too, so a new spine could not be built on it:** `Proverbs 11:1` appears on **6** weeks' anchors, `Deuteronomy 19:15` on **7**, `Leviticus 19:36` on **3**, `Luke 14:28` on **8**, `Proverbs 27:23` on **6**. Those are the standing register, not available as an anchor.

**Then the free ground, counted rather than guessed at.** Occurrences across all 48 prior weeks, on the anchors and in the full module text: `Genesis 23` (any verse) **0**, `Machpelah` **0**, `Ephron` **0**, `Ruth 4` **0**, `Boaz` **0**, `Jeremiah 32` **0**, `Hanameel` **0**, `Luke 19:8` **0**, `Zacchaeus` **0**, `Mark 12:41`–`12:44` **0**, `two mites` **0**, `Matthew 10:29`/`10:30` **0**, `2 Samuel 24:24` **0**, `Araunah` **0**, `Isaiah 55:1` **0**, `Psalms 49:7`/`49:8` **0**, `1 Corinthians 6:20` **0**, `Acts 20:28` **0**, `Revelation 5:9` **0**, `bought with a price` **0**, `Proverbs 20:14` **0**, `Proverbs 22:1` **0**.

So the untaught seam is **THE NAMED, SPOKEN, WITNESSED, RECORDED PURCHASE** — not who may spend, which this course has settled three times, but what a transaction IS in the Word — and the spine is **Genesis 23 + Ruth 4 + Jeremiah 32 + Luke 19:8 + Mark 12:41-44 + 2 Samuel 24:24 + the purchase with a Name on it for ever**.

**The fit is exact, and the article hands it over itself.** Its own closing section is titled "when every customer is a stranger", and it says the quiet part without being pressed: the seller receives a public key and nothing else, so **"payment is no longer a form of identification"**; there is no account, so no abuse history and nobody to disable; no signup record; no refund flow defined at all; and a capped key "doesn't stop an agent from spending correctly on the wrong things." Then the sentence this lesson is named after — that even where a seller *wants* to offer a better service, **there is nobody to contact after the transaction is done**. The industry's answer, the piece reports, is to add identity and disputes back as separate layers beside the payment. That is the name being re-attached afterwards as an optional module, having been removed from the transaction by design. **The Word's order is the reverse, and the reversal is the lesson.**

Abraham's purchase is five requirements in one verse, and only the last of them is protocol-shaped: the silver **weighed** rather than asserted, paid to **Ephron**, a named man rather than an address, at a figure **named in the audience of the sons of Heth** before it was paid, a **stated** four hundred shekels, in **current money with the merchant** — an agreed standard of value, and the least of the five. Then the clause the chapter states twice: the field was **made sure** "in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that went in at the gate of his city." The Word never says Abraham got a receipt. It says he got a city full of witnesses, and those are different objects: **a receipt attests that a payment happened; a witness can be gone to afterwards.** Boaz adds what no header can carry — the **purpose** declared inside the purchase, "to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance" — and the town answers him, "We are witnesses." And Jeremiah, in prison in a besieged city with the captivity certain, files the most careful record in Scripture: subscribed, sealed, witnessed, weighed in the balances, **one copy sealed so it could not be altered and one open so it could be read**, handed to a named man before four audiences, and stored in an earthen vessel "that they may continue many days." Yahweh then makes that dull closing the sign of a people brought home: "Men shall buy fields for money, and subscribe evidences, and seal them, and take witnesses." Set that beside the article's own line that the next time an agent needs something it starts from zero, and there are two theories of what a record is for.

The three things that have no substitute once the person is gone are named plainly, because each is engineering rather than nostalgia: **restitution** needs somebody to restore TO (Zacchaeus restores a particular *him*, fourfold); **a reputation** cannot be carried by a key that is rotated per deployment and revoked on suspicion, and the Word prices a good name above great riches; and **honest dealing** is a matter of the heart no verified payload reaches — the article's own second guardrail is a seller quoting one price in the friendly description and another in the signed payload, and verifying the payload catches the lie in the number while never touching the man who wrote it.

Then the close inverts the article's hardest practical problem. A cent is not worth settling, so bundle it. **Yahweh's accounting runs the other way:** He "beheld how the people cast money into the treasury", which is not totalling what they cast; He counted two mites, "which make a farthing", comfortably below any economic threshold; He knew what the widow had left; He prices two sparrows at a farthing and numbers the hairs. And He refuses what cost nothing — David pays fifty shekels for a threshingfloor he was offered free. The one market in all the Word that charges nothing is not frictionless, because somebody else paid: the redemption of a soul was beyond us, and He purchased with His own blood, "out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation." **He did not buy a volume. He bought people, by name, at a stated price, before witnesses, and the deed is sealed and will continue many days.**

## Impact

- The forty-ninth week of Sovereign A.I. teaches what a transaction IS in the Word, on ground no other week in the course holds, and **names** weeks 13, 17, 19, 29, 31, 37, 42 and 45 so a reader is sent to them rather than served any of them a sixth time. The test asserts that naming, so the courtesy cannot quietly fall out.
- **The verses are generated, not typed.** `scripts/sov49-fill.mjs` holds the prose with `[[Book C:V]]` placeholders and fills each one from `app/public/bible/kjv` at build time, then derives `anchor.ref` from the same placeholders — so a quotation cannot be approximate, and DR-0734 holds in both directions (every verse quoted is on the anchor; every verse on the anchor is quoted). **37 references, 135 quoted spans, zero verbatim faults.**
- **The claims are sorted in three tiers per DR-0100 and taught that way.** ESTABLISHED by the report and stated plainly rather than hedged: the design removes the person deliberately; the seller gets a key and nothing more; payment is no longer identification; no account, no abuse history, no refund flow. OPEN and named narrowly: whether this becomes the standard, its real volumes, its settled fees, and its standards-body status on the day the page is read — the report gives a launch date, a transaction count and a standards track, and **nobody here checked any of them**, so they are reported, not established. Its two statistics (a share of web requests that are automated, attributed to one network operator's report; a one-month transaction count) are likewise reported, and the argument deliberately does not depend on either, because the *design* is the subject and the design is described by its own authors. OVER-REACH corrected both ways: that a believer should refuse payment technology altogether, which the Word contradicts by recording purchases, weighings and deeds approvingly — and the costlier one, that nothing has been lost because nothing has gone wrong yet.
- **The two sponsored segments are named as advertising and used for nothing** — a monitoring vendor's booklet on automated site-reliability work, and a webinar about a context layer for coding agents. Not one sentence of the lesson rests on either, and the quiz asks the class what was done with them.
- All four age bands are authored from the first commit (child 4,844 / youth 6,646 / teen 13,258 / senior 11,623 characters against a 26,981-character lesson), so `adultOnly` and `adultRegister` both stay 0 and the `sovereign-ai` row reads `{lessons: 49, allFour: 28}`.
- TALK ABOUT IT TOGETHER closes the lesson **and every band separately**, in the lesson's own words, all three directions, each with the skill (ask, listen to the end, retell, teach one verse) and the rhythm (once today in one of Deuteronomy 6:7's four places; one friend this week), and the growth measured the Word's way — the fruit (Galatians 5:22), the occasions (Deuteronomy 6:7) and the days (Hebrews 3:13).

## Decision

**sov49 ships on the measured-free spine; its verses are generated from the corpus rather than typed; and its test pins the two faults that were caught in its own draft.**

- **37 verses**, every one fetched from `app/public/bible/kjv` and pinned against it, with **135 quoted spans verified verbatim** across the lesson, the four bands, `bigIdea`, `title`, `inApp`, the anchor theme, the `rpe` block, the benefits, both stories, the ten facilitator talking points, `howToRun`, the ten discussion prompts, and every quiz question, option and explanation — not only the prose a reader scrolls.
- **The DR-0210 bright line is pinned per field, in both directions.** `God` and `the LORD` appear **zero** times in our own prose and only inside quotations, where the KJV's wording is left exactly as written; `Yahweh` appears **27** times in ours. Ruth 4:11, Jeremiah 32:14, 2 Samuel 24:24, Isaiah 55:1, Psalms 49:7, 1 Corinthians 6:20, Acts 20:28, John 1:29, John 3:16 and Hebrews 1:8 all carry `God` or `the LORD` inside the quotation, which is exactly where they stay. **The check also asserts an even count of double quotes per field**, because an odd one silently mis-pairs the strip and the whole bright-line case then measures the wrong text.
- **A substitution into a near-quotation was caught in this lesson's own first draft and is recorded here, not hidden.** The tenth movement read "unto Yahweh of that which doth cost me nothing" — our covenant name pushed into an echo of 2 Samuel 24:24. It was rewritten to our own words ("He would not bring Yahweh an offering that had cost him nothing") before the test file existed. Five near-verbatim quotations in quiz explanations were converted to `[[ref]]` placeholders for the same reason: an unquoted echo is outside the span checker's reach, so it is not allowed to be a quotation.
- **Both stories are parables and say so.** Neither is a named person's consented account, so neither may claim to be one — the correction sov47 had to make, caught by `a-true-story-names-whose-life-it-was`.
- **The quiz's right answer is not always the first option.** sov47 and sov48 both put every correct answer at index 0, which is a pattern a learner can pass without reading; the test now requires more than one distinct answer slot.

## Verification

- **14 cases green**, and **4 proven to catch** by mutation (DR-0076 §3), restored to 14 green after each:
  1. Changing `four hundred shekels` to `five hundred` inside the child band's quotation of Genesis 23:16 reddened "every quoted span ... is that verse verbatim" and named the field (`child: Genesis 23:16`).
  2. Turning the curly apostrophe straight inside `rpe.plan`'s quotation of Ruth 4:9 (`Elimelech’s` → `Elimelech's`) reddened BOTH the span case and the dedicated apostrophe case, naming the field and all five offending windows — the sov47 defect class, which this lesson is exposed to through Ruth 4:9, Jeremiah 32:9, Jeremiah 32:12 and 1 Corinthians 6:20.
  3. Stripping the friend line out of the teen band alone made `placesMissingDirections` name `teen` and `missingDirections` return `friends`, **while the pooled `hasAllThree` stayed green** — the exact divergence DR-0795 exists for, asserted on the real text rather than on a fixture.
  4. The array-hole case (`},,` leaving an `undefined` in the catalog) is carried forward from sov48, where the splice actually did it; the generator now excises the preceding comma with the block on `--rebuild` so the rebuild path cannot reproduce it.
- **Band measurements, from the real text rather than estimated.** Lesson-to-band 8-word shingle overlap: child 0.328, youth 0.350, teen 0.439, senior 0.421 — all under the 0.5 ceiling, so the lesson body is not a band wearing a second label (the sov48 defect, which read 0.995). Band-to-band: 0.280 to 0.414.
- **DR-1185, measured:** the most verses sov49 shares with any other week in the course is **6** (sov41), against a threshold of 10, and the six are the course's standing confession and growth register (John 1:29, John 3:16, Hebrews 1:8, Deuteronomy 6:7, Galatians 5:22, Hebrews 3:13). `one-teaching-one-lesson-guard` passes.
- `sovereign-ai-class.test.js` (22 cases) green with `HELD_IN_FLIGHT` **unchanged at `[]`**: weeks 1..49 ascend on disk with no gap, so no hold is recorded and none is discharged.
- `sovereign-ai-verse-integrity.test.js` (203 cases), `course-band-coverage.test.js` (23), `course-bands-reach-the-reader.test.js` (39), `band-differentiation-gate.test.js` (18), `talk-together.test.js` (16), `four-band-ladder`, `four-band-group-c`, `course-four-bands-group-a`, `course-four-bands-hold`, `the-band-you-pick-is-what-you-read` and `the-band-excuse-list-only-shrinks` all green.
- `npm run lint` clean; `npm run verify:gates` clean, including `one-teaching-one-lesson-guard` and `lesson-dates:check`.
- **The full Vitest suite is delegated to CI** and was not run locally: several builders share one local memory-slot mutex tonight, and waiting on it starves them.

## What this does not do

- It does **not** re-teach the delegated key with a cap, an expiry and a recipient list (weeks 19, 29, 31), who owns the rails (week 13), paying a worker the same day (week 42), the just weight (weeks 17, 37), or how many witnesses establish a matter (week 45). Those weeks are named on the page so a reader is sent, and left alone so the course does not say one thing six times.
- It does **not** claim the protocol exists as described beyond what the newsletter reports. The specification was not read here, no standards-body record was opened, no transaction was priced, and no figure was confirmed against a primary document. **That limit is stated on the page before the teaching, not in a footnote.**
- It does **not** condemn the engineering. The design is given its due in a full movement, because a steward cannot govern what he cannot describe, and the instruction is to build it well — scope the key, cap the spend, keep the receipts — and to refuse only the lesson a nameless transaction teaches the heart.
- It does **not** take anything from the issue's advertising, and it does not treat the article's statistics as established.
- It adds **no** autonomous or timer-driven behaviour, so the three-brakes rule is not engaged.
